props.title: No One Killed Jessica
props.initialSlug: The truth will set her free.

sections.content: **No One Killed Jessica** (2011) marks a pivotal moment in Indian cinema's approach to true-crime storytelling. Based on the infamous Jessica Lal murder case, director Raj Kumar Gupta crafted a searing indictment of India's justice system that shares DNA with **Talvar** (2015) and **Black Friday** (2004). The film's raw portrayal of media activism and public outrage echoes similar themes in **Spotlight** (2015), though through a distinctly Indian lens where class privilege and corruption intertwine. Section 375|2019|A courtroom drama examining sexual assault allegations against a filmmaker, challenging perceptions of truth and justice|Netflix Talvar|2015|Based on the 2008 Noida double murder case, following an investigator's pursuit of truth amid media circus|Disney+ Article 15|2019|A police officer confronts caste discrimination while investigating missing girls in rural India|Netflix

The dual performances of Rani Mukerji as the fierce journalist Meera and Vidya Balan as Jessica's grieving sister Sabrina create a powerful dynamic rarely seen in Indian mainstream cinema. Their approach recalls the determined investigation in **Zodiac** (2007), where obsession with justice drives the narrative. The film's structure, alternating between investigation and personal impact, influenced later Indian true-crime films like **Raazi** (2018) and **Talaash** (2012).

What sets **No One Killed Jessica** apart is its unflinching examination of media trial and public activism. Like **Network** (1976), it shows how television can mobilize public conscience, though here it's used for justice rather than ratings. The film's portrayal of real-life events mirrors the approach of **Z** (1969), where political thriller elements enhance rather than overshadow the truth. Mumbai Meri Jaan|2008|Interweaving stories following the aftermath of Mumbai train bombings|Prime Shahid|2013|Biopic of lawyer Shahid Azmi who defended those wrongly accused of terrorism|Netflix SUBHEAD: Media Activism and Social Justice

The film's impact on Indian cinema's treatment of investigative journalism can't be overstated. It paved the way for hard-hitting exposés like **Madaari** (2016) and **Rann** (2010). The way it captures media's role in social justice movements predicted the rise of social media activism, though it focuses on traditional journalism's power to effect change.
